sections.title: How I prepare
paragraphs: I refresh the stack I actually used: Playwright, API, SQL, CI, and how I explain the QA process.
I keep two versions of answers. Ukrainian is how I think. English is spoken: short sentences, one idea each, with real technical words (fixtures, storageState, 401).
I practice the story of the work, not only tool names: first QA on a project, what I automated and why, how I look for a root cause.

sections.title: What I am learning now
paragraphs: Interview prep around Playwright: fixtures, storageState, APIRequest, locators that stay stable, why a test is flaky.
How to explain a framework and Jenkins jobs (merge request, branch, nightly) in a clear way.
Spoken English for work answers. My level is Intermediate / B1. I say that honestly.
SQL and API checks for defect investigation.

sections.title: Playwright — short conspect
paragraphs: This is my main automation stack now: TypeScript and Playwright. I use it for UI, API (APIRequest), and end-to-end flows.
Framework shape I use: OOP, page objects, fixtures. Login is not repeated in every test when storageState can hold the session (cookies / auth).
I look at locators, frames, parallel runs, and flaky tests as part of the job, not as a surprise at the end.
I also used Java, Selenium, and Maven in commercial work at RIA.com. At Clear Junction and FRACTAL I used TypeScript and Playwright. Playwright is what I use today.

sections.title: What I automate
paragraphs: I automate flows that run often and must stay green in CI: regression, critical UI + API paths, repeated setup.
A useful automated test is one the team can trust after a merge.

sections.title: How I use Cursor
paragraphs: I use Cursor every day in automation work. It is a speed tool, not the owner of the test. I read every generated change before I merge: locators, waits, test data, and whether the assertion hits a real risk.

Refactoring: I use it to extract page objects, fixtures, and helpers, and to kill duplicated locators. The draft can come from the agent. I still check that the POM public API stays clear and that tests assert the same thing as before.

Debugging: I paste a Playwright trace, a CI log, a network call, or an API body and ask for hypotheses. I do not accept “add a wait” as a fix. I confirm the cause in DevTools, the API response, or SQL, then change the locator, the data, or the environment.

Ideas and artifacts: I brainstorm coverage gaps, negative API cases, and EP / BVA edges. I also get first drafts of test cases, checklists, bug reports, test-plan outlines, and RCA notes. I edit them before they go to the team.
Reports: from Allure or a Jenkins run I ask for a short failure grouping — flake vs product vs test data — then I write the note the team can act on.

How I keep it useful: project rules so new tests follow our POM and fixtures, not a generic Playwright sample. Boilerplate for a page, a fixture, APIRequest, or storageState is fine. I reject brittle CSS and “self-healing” locators. Stable roles, labels, and test ids stay my decision. I also turn a manual checklist into an automation outline, then I choose what is worth putting in CI.
